name: What is the difference between retrofitting an existing window and framing for an enlarged opening?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between retrofitting an existing window and framing for an enlarged opening?

acceptedAnswer.text: Framing for window enlargement requires removing the old header and rebuilding the rough opening completely, whereas a simple insert replacement uses the existing frame. With insert windows, the original framing and exterior siding remain untouched. Enlarging an opening—whether making it wider or dropping the sill lower—requires opening drywall down to the studs, assessing structural loads, installing a longer, sturdier header with new jack studs, and modifying exterior siding. While enlargement provides greater natural light and updated layouts, it involves a significantly larger scope of framing, drywall repair, and finish carpentry.
acceptedAnswer.description: Retrofitting fits a new window into existing framing, while enlarging requires tearing out old studs, installing a larger header, and redoing surrounding drywall and trim.
